title: Toy Commander
subtitle: The house becomes a battlefield
summary: Toy Commander is No Cliché's action game, first released for Dreamcast in Europe on 14 October 1999.
body: Toy Commander is No Cliché's action game, first released for Dreamcast in Europe on 14 October 1999. A child's new military toys face a rebellion by older favourites led by Huggy Bear. The player controls miniature vehicles through missions set around the house, where kitchens and bedrooms become enormous landscapes. Director Frédérick Raynal's team builds the challenges around those domestic surroundings. A familiar object can become a destination, an obstacle or part of the task, making the difference in scale central to how each mission is understood and completed.

The vehicles include racing cars, armed trucks and tanks, aircraft, helicopters and unarmed transports. Switching between them changes what the player can reach or carry. An early kitchen mission teaches several types in succession, while another asks a toy car to roll eggs towards a pot of boiling water. Such tasks give the vehicles purposes beyond firing at one another. The player must inspect the room, recognise which object matters and choose a toy whose movement or equipment can turn the household arrangement into a workable route.

The old toys hold different areas of the house, providing the main campaign with opponents tied to its rooms. Multiplayer modes also allow up to four people to battle locally, turning the same miniature machinery into a shared contest. Philippe Vachey's music accompanies the journey. The setting gives Toy Commander its strongest connection between appearance and play: the rooms remain recognisable as places in a home, while a small vehicle experiences their furniture, containers and surfaces as the geography of a much larger adventure.
